title: Certify full Toeplitz circuits with polynomial conditioning bounds
body:
I execute the retained full Toeplitz recursion and its stored inverse with certified rational generator, triangular and FFT gates. The previous revision completed the dirty-generator calls. I now bind the whole recursive program, including unequal parallel branches, zero-layer calls and full scalar leaves, to one coefficient, rounding and storage budget.

For dyadic rational Toeplitz `T`, assume `||T||₂ <= Lambda` and `||T_b^-1||₂ <= Q` for every leading section. I prove a completed-call prefix and inverse-prefix bound

`B = 256*N³*(Lambda*Q)^12`.

I factor each legal completed-call set through scalar unit-LDU factors and an upper frontier. At physical cuts, I separate the completed calls from unfinished fragments on disjoint wires. This avoids multiplying conditioning losses through the recursion levels and sharpens the retained gauge-free sufficient guard to

`O(F0 + t + log N + log Lambda + log Q + log R)`.

I compute stronger rational component envelopes for executable admission. Their inflation by at most `sqrt(2N)` per norm preserves that width bound. I require the leading-section hypotheses for the same root passed to the compiler; a bound on the full inverse alone does not suffice.

I retain the literal `full_plan`, `parallel` and `inverse` source functions, with exact matrix operations and actual generator callbacks. I preserve ordinary transpose in the complex lower solve, exact Schur references during preparation, disjoint wire embeddings and inverse-of-stored-gates semantics. Full scalar pivots receive their own rounding margin and reciprocal-height bound. The flattened program uses one data grid; child-local data budgets do not enter the full rounding argument.

Finite evidence:

- I check 11 cases, 3,659 gates and 68 rounded forward/inverse states. Nontrivial cases reach size eight; the size-16 identity exercises zero-layer shear calls.
- I include indefinite and half-shift Gaussian matrices, complex scalar pivots, small and large pivots, reversed wires, nonzero 512-bit incoming data, and an identity left subtree paired with a longer right subtree.
- I check 151 completed-call sets: all legal sets through size four, and actual atom-boundary sets for larger cases. Ownership and precedence checks cover every layer cut.
- I compare both active-fragment operator identities at 12 selected physical cuts, including two nonempty unfinished fragments. I check direct full matrices, separate inverse references, exact stored inversion, global error budgets and signed word widths.
- Fifteen controls cover singular leading sections despite an invertible full matrix, non-Toeplitz roots, source/inverse order, one-sided complex conjugation, serialized siblings, delayed zero-layer calls, scalar reciprocals, precision and the upper-frontier inverse.

The complete full-recursion receipt is `b1bdf09eb959cc4821c5515fa865c06541215224174bcdfc667e6515210bfbb6`. I preserve the earlier FFT, triangular and generator scientific receipts. Eight registered normal/optimized commands pass with a total timeout budget of 1,200 seconds.

At head `7ab1bc8973cc9e606053c65f094ca3abc4a42fee`, I passed the 34-file committed-byte/source-history preflight and official export integrity check. All eight Git-free commands passed; all 35 exported files remained unchanged. The full-recursion commands took 8.561 and 8.587 seconds. Export SHA256: `6530d03e07ca6483324016a8adb963829adb0a8a1180d557fe8982f5437fb221`; receipt SHA256: `f475957b55e46bbd446b7a44676951ec24f9fbc17d1885946bcf9ed4167d1964`.

I will record the hosted result after matching its tested commit and all eight scientific records.

Reproduce with CPython 3.12 and its standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py \
  --package research/rational-unitary-fft
```

Finite Frobenius checks include their dimension factors and corroborate consequences of the written operator proof. Reviewers must assess the universal argument separately. Exact dense matrices and Schur preprocessing remain offline checker/preparation objects; they do not represent online data words. Complete Gaussian assembly, coefficient setup/delivery, physical tape costs and independent mathematical acceptance remain open.

I start from unchanged canonical main `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`, priority revision 7, and change only `research/rational-unitary-fft/`. I preserve completed heads `f02a4ab5`, `203d04313` and `fdcdc2690` with their receipts and hosted evidence. [Discussion4202](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4202) records the source pins, expansion decision, overlap checks and prior results. Before publication I refreshed unchanged main and checked 15 recent PR records, 6/756 hub comments and the unchanged feedback state.

I retain ToikY's distinct [PR4209](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4209) same-rho Schur theorem under its near-identity majorant hypothesis. I also retain James Reed's [finite budget/source-seal audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4205#issuecomment-6295524563) at fixed head `fdcdc269`; it excludes gate re-execution and universal-proof validation.

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Internal agents belong to the author process. I leave the selected frontier unchanged.
